newsitem.title: JAPAN: Bandai chief resigns symbolically as merger failed.
newsitem.headline: Bandai chief resigns symbolically as merger failed.

text.p: Japanese toymaker Bandai Co Ltd said on Wednesday that its president intends to step aside to take the responsibility for the bungling of a planned merger with Sega Enterprises Ltd.
However, the firm said that while giving up the presidency, Makoto Yamashina plans to stay on with the company as chairman.

"We have not made any formal decision. But we've confirmed that President Yamashina personally intends to resign to become chairman in order to take the responsibility for the cancellation of the merger," a Bandai official told Reuters.
Bandai, known for its "Power Rangers" series and virtual pet toy "Tamagotchi", may make a formal decision on the personnel change at a board meeting on Thursday, the official said.
On Tuesday, just a day before the two firms were due to sign a merger contract, they announced they had called off the deal after strong opposition from mid-level Bandai managers.
They said that instead of a merger, the two firms would pursue a business tie-up covering the sharing of entertainment characters, retailing, consumer products, manufacturing and distribution.
Yamashina said on Tuesday that there were "huge differences in the two corporate cultures", and that the merger lacked the synergy needed to make it work.
He said then that he had no plans to step down.
Sega, maker of the Sega Saturn 32-bit video-game player, and Bandai said in January that they would merge to create a global entertainment giant they likened to Walt Disney Co.
Bandai shares fell on Wednesday as a result of the merger cancellation and after the Tokyo market closed the firm announced poor earnings for last business year to March 31.
Bandai said it plunged into the red on a group basis and posted a group net loss of 7.98 billion yen ($68.7 million), having achieved a profit of 10.36 billion yen ($89.3 million) the previous year.
Bandai shares ended the day down 90 yen at 2,670, while Sega was 80 yen firmer at 3,780.

Despite last year's poor figures, Bandai said it would return to profit in the current business year. It said it would manage a group net profit of 2.5 billion yen ($21.5 million) helped by the runaway success of "Tamagotchi", a toy featuring an electronic pet bird.
The toy became an instant hit after its debut in November, and about five million units have already been shipped. ($1=116 yen)
